'''Claire Miller''' (née '''Claire Ann Ferguson''') is a Scottish [[environmental statistics|environmental statistician]], a professor of statistics in the School of Mathematics and Statistics at the [[University of Glasgow]], and a former president of the International Environmetrics Society.{{r|staff}} Her research focuses on statistical models of [[water quality]].{{r|aes|barnett}}

==Education and career==
Miller was a student at the University of Glasgow, where she received first class honours in mathematics and statistics in 2003,{{r|gug}} and continued for a Ph.D. in 2007. Her dissertation, ''Univariate and multivariate statistical methodologies for lake ecosystem modelling'', was jointly supervised by Adrian Bowman and [[Marian Scott (statistician)|Marian Scott]].{{r|diss}}

She has been a member of the academic staff at the University of Glasgow since 2007.{{r|orcid}}

==Recognition==
Miller became an Elected Member of the [[International Statistical Institute]] in 2015, and belonged to the [[Young Academy of Scotland]] of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]] from 2016 to 2021. She served as president of the International Environmetrics Society from 2023 to 2025.{{r|staff}}

She was the 2018 recipient of the Abdel El-Shaarawi Early Investigator's Award of the International Environmetrics Society, "for outstanding contributions to environmental statistical and quantitative research with a special focus on water quality, including functional data, [[time series]] clustering and dimension reduction for spatiotemporal flow-connected network data".{{r|aes}} In 2025 she received the Barnett Award of the [[Royal Statistical Society]] for "exceptional contributions to environmental statistics" and "pioneering work in water quality measuring, monitoring and forecasting".{{r|barnett}}
